summary.description: AOXs are a large group of organic compounds primarily containing chlorine, and sometimes iodine or bromine. Most AOXs are not intentionally manufactured and have diverse chemical structures.
emission_sources: Chlorine-containing bleaches and disinfectants reacting with organic matter
environmental_impact: Some AOXs are toxic to aquatic life even at low concentrations
Many AOXs persist in the environment due to their chemical stability
AOXs have a tendency to bio-accumulate and concentrate up the food chain

top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: AOXs contaminate water bodies through industrial and bleaching processes, threatening water quality and sanitation.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: Toxicity and bioaccumulation of AOXs severely affect aquatic organisms and ecosystems.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Exposure to AOXs, depending on the compound, poses health risks including toxicity and long-term effects due to persistence and bioaccumulation.
